protocols.airplayServer: AirPlay: receive audio from iPhone, iPad and Mac
protocols.airplayClient: AirPlay: send audio to AirPlay speakers
protocols.matineeServer: Matinee: shows up in Matinee as a player and plays what it's sent
protocols.matineeClient: Matinee: play on a Matinee player (address: the player's id)
protocols.streamClient: Stream: a live WAV stream for VLC or a browser
protocols.radioServer: Internet radio: play a station, playlist or audio file from a URL
protocols.pulseServer: PipeWire or PulseAudio: record a line-in, a USB audio interface or a phone playing over Bluetooth
protocols.castClient: Google Cast: play on Chromecast, Nest and Google Home speakers, speaker groups and Cast TVs
protocols.pulseClient: PipeWire or PulseAudio: play on a sound card or a paired Bluetooth speaker
protocols.snapcastClient: Snapcast: play in sync on every Snapcast client
protocols.upnpServer: UPnP/DLNA: shows up as a speaker in DLNA apps, such as BubbleUPnP, and plays what they send
protocols.upnpClient: UPnP/DLNA: play on Sonos, AV receivers, smart TVs and other DLNA renderers
protocols.bluetoothServer: Bluetooth: shows up as a Bluetooth speaker that phones and laptops pair with
protocols.spotifyServer: Spotify Connect: shows up as a speaker in the Spotify app
protocols.airplay2Server: AirPlay 2: shows up as an AirPlay 2 speaker on iPhone, iPad and Mac, including multi-room
protocols.airplay2Client: AirPlay 2 (experimental): play on HomePods, Apple TVs and other AirPlay 2 speakers

servers.title: Sources
servers.what: Where audio comes from: a speaker your phone plays to over AirPlay, Bluetooth or Spotify Connect, a radio station, a line-in and more.
servers.addHint: A source is where audio comes from. An AirPlay source shows up as an AirPlay speaker on your iPhone, iPad or Mac.
servers.interfaceHint: Leave empty or write "auto" to detect it. Name an interface, such as en0 or eth0, if detection picks the wrong one.
servers.empty: No sources yet. Add one to start.
servers.deleteMessage: The source is removed for good, and speakers stop playing it.

clients.title: Speakers
clients.what: Where audio plays. Pick what each speaker plays, or select several to play one source on all of them.
clients.addHint: Find speakers on your network, or set one up by hand if it isn't found.
clients.empty: No speakers yet. Add one to start.
clients.deleteMessage: The speaker is removed for good.
clients.sourceFailed: Couldn't change what the speaker plays

routes.title: Routes
routes.what: What the speaker cards are made of: each route sends one source to one or more speakers. Add routes here to mix several sources into one speaker or to set a source's level. A route plays only while it's on.
routes.addHint: A route sends one source to one or more speakers. Routes into the same speaker are mixed.
routes.deleteMessage: The route is removed for good.

discovery.title: Find devices
discovery.searchingLong: Looking for devices on your network
discovery.none: No devices found. Set one up by hand below.
discovery.noneHint: Make sure your devices are on the same network and try again, or set one up by hand below.
discovery.failed: Couldn't look for devices. Set one up by hand below.
discovery.selectFailed: Couldn't pick that device. Find devices again, or set it up by hand.
discovery.manualHint: Use this if your device wasn't found.

fields.urlHint: An internet radio station, a playlist (.pls, .m3u, .m3u8) or an audio file. A file plays on repeat.
fields.sourceHint: A source's name or description, the Bluetooth address of a phone playing to this machine, or a sink's name followed by .monitor. Leave empty for the default source.
fields.sinkHint: A sink's name or description, or a Bluetooth speaker's address such as AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF. Leave empty for the default sink.
fields.pulseServerHint: Leave empty for the usual one on this machine.
fields.delayHint: Holds audio back to line this speaker up with slower ones.
fields.sampleRateHint: The rate in the snapserver source's sampleformat. Leave empty for 48000, snapserver's default.
fields.snapcastAddressHint: The snapserver host, and the port of its TCP source if it isn't 4953.
fields.castAddressHint: The device's IP address, and its port if it isn't 8009 (speaker groups use another port). Cast devices play a few seconds late, so delay other speakers to match.
fields.listenHint: The port apps reach this input on, such as :49494. Leave empty for a free port.
fields.upnpAddressHint: The renderer's description URL, as Find Devices gives it, or a Sonos player's IP address.
fields.formatHint: wav or mp3. Leave empty for MP3 on Sonos and WAV on everything else. MP3 needs ffmpeg.
fields.btDeviceHint: Record only this phone, by Bluetooth address. Leave empty to record whichever device plays.
fields.btHidden: Hidden: only phones already paired can connect
fields.airplay2PortHint: The port AirPlay 2 listens on, such as :7000. Give each AirPlay input its own port.
fields.airplay2AddressHint: The receiver's address and port, as Find Devices gives it, such as 192.168.1.60:7000. It must allow anyone on the network to play, without a password.

pairing.title: AirPlay Pairing
pairing.required: This Apple TV needs to be paired before it can be used. Enter the 4-digit PIN it shows on screen.
pairing.prompt: Enter the PIN your Apple TV shows
pairing.pinHelp: The 4-digit code on your Apple TV's screen
pairing.badPin: Enter the 4 digits your Apple TV shows.
pairing.noClient: There's no client to pair. Add it again.
pairing.doneMessage: The device is paired and ready to use.

matinee.title: Matinee
matinee.what: Connect Air-Mixer to your Matinee server and its players become speakers here (Add Speaker finds them), and Matinee sources show up in Matinee and Home Assistant as players. Sign in once, the way you sign in a TV: approve the code on Matinee's /link page as an admin.
matinee.approve: Open {{url}} as a Matinee admin and enter {{code}}. Waiting for approval…
matinee.signedInMessage: Matinee players now show up in Add Speaker
matinee.notConnected: Not connected to a Matinee server.
